text:
sam: Quick sanity check: ran a regional latency heatmap for quantized-2bit variante on A100 vs H100 across us-east/us-west/eu-west. p50 looks fine but p95 in eu-west is ~240ms and p99 jumps to ~1.2s when edge routes fall back. cc @julia @neil
julia: Can you paste the heatmap link and which kernel selected? saw weird tail when fallback triggered last week. :thinking:
sam: Link: https://redwood-internal/charts/regional-heatmap/1871234567 (only accessible internally). Kernel chosen by runtime: auto -> fell back from fused_flash_attention to slower_fp16_conv when KV cache > 3.
neil: Ugh that fallback ordering bites for shortish seqs. Do we have per-region kernel histogram?
sam: Yes, extracted per-pop kernel counts: us-east {fused: 78%, flash: 12%, slow_fp16:10%}, us-west {fused: 65%, flash: 20%, slow_fp16:15%}, eu-west {fused: 40%, flash: 25%, slow_fp16:35%}. p95/p99 correlate with slow_fp16%.
anna: Important detail — the eu-west POP hits a proxy that strips gRPC keepalive, so the serving runtime sees slightly longer cold calls and forces a different KV sharding which increases KV size per request. That pushes kernel selection.
julia: Suggest two quick mitigations: 1) change routing policy to prefer local-pop strong affinity (reduce fallthrough) for production model, 2) tweak kernel selection threshold (force fused path up to KV size 6). Which is less risky?
neil: Policy change is safer short-term. Kernel threshold touches low-level runtime - need perf tests. Also re-run bench with smaller batch sizes to mirror PL traffic.
sam: I ran a micro-bench: rbench --model q2bit-13b --gpu A100 --region eu-west --seq 128 --batch 1..8 --kernels auto,force_fused and captured p50/p95/p99. Sample output:```csv
gpu,region,kernel,batch,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms
A100,eu-west,auto,1,45,230,1200
A100,eu-west,force_fused,1,50,110,160
H100,eu-west,auto,1,40,95,130
```
sam: Force_fused reduced tail massively but slightly increased p50. tradeoff looks fine.
anna: Ops note — if we change routing to stronger local affinity, capacity sizing for eu-west needs +20% headroom because it will absorb more requests.
julia: For canary: do routing policy at 25% traffic to eu-west local-first, monitor p95 and cost. If good after 4h, ramp. Also open quick runtime PR to adjust kernel threshold but gate it behind an opt-in flag.
neil: I'll own the canary run. Plan: patch routing, start canary at 10:00 UTC, run 4h, collect p50/p95/p99 and kernel distribution, then decide.
ops-bot: incident: latency-spike-eu-west detected 1871234550 -> auto-created ticket INF-4921, linked.
deploy-bot: started rollout routing-policy/eu-local-affinity canary -> id r-9812
sam: logs during canary show p95 eu-west dropped from ~240ms to ~120ms within 6 minutes of canary start. p99 dropped from ~1.2s to ~180ms.
julia: Nice. Neil please upload a short note to the runbook about the proxy gRPC keepalive issue so platforms can fix long-term.
neil: Will do. Also adding a perf dashboard panel for kernel breakdown per-pop.\samanthabot: reminder: weekly infra sync tomorrow 14:00 UTC. :bell:
sam: TL;DR: fallback-induced kernel selection in eu-west created p99 tail. Short-term: routing affinity canary + capacity + opt-in kernel threshold. Medium: proxy fix and runtime default tweak behind flag. Everyone ok with that plan? :thumbsup:
julia: +1
neil: +1
anna: +1
ops-bot: resolved alert INF-4921 (suppressed after canary)
deploy-bot: canary completed, id r-9812 -> success
sam: Thanks all, closing thread.
